goal.title: Game notices say what changed
criteria: Switching a game between play and review mode notifies its listeners, and the notice says it was a mode switch; switching to the mode it is already in sends nothing.
Checking out a branch, rewinding (by the tool or the board's jump) and undoing each send a notice naming that kind of change; new events send a notice with no change kind, as today.
Ending a turn on the board in play mode returns the same prompt text as before, now built by the game.
Open boards still refresh on every kind of notice, including a mode switch made by the assistant.

items.title: The presence and the turn wait

goal.title: The presence and the turn wait
criteria: A wait on the player's seat ends within a fraction of a second of that seat ending its turn, reporting the new turn, whose turn it is, the hand-off text and the point the player's moves start from.
In review mode, a turn ending for the other seat does not end a wait on the handed-over seat.

With no player activity for the check-in time, the wait reports a check-in. Activity more often than that never triggers one. The next call after a check-in starts a fresh clock, or reports the turn as ended if the player ended it meanwhile.
A mode switch, a new or replaced game, an expired game, a branch checkout and a rewind each end the wait with the matching reason, whether they happen during a call or between calls.
No call lasts longer than the cap. A second call takes over from one still in flight, and a cancelled call returns at once.
After many waits that time out, get cancelled, get superseded or end on game changes, the game's listeners, the presence's timers and the running goroutines are back where they started.

goal.title: The wait_for_turn tool
criteria: Over both the desktop and hosted connections, the tool reports each outcome with its seat, the next cursor, the log lines in the view `get_log` would use, and a `next` line saying what to do.

In play mode the tool waits only on the player's seat, and refuses a fresh wait during the assistant's own turn when nothing is pending; in review mode it waits on the named seat or the seat whose turn it is.
The tool finds its game through the quiet resolver when one is set, and through the normal lookup otherwise.
The standing instructions tell the assistant to wait after handing over a turn, to ask exactly "Still playing?" on a check-in, and never to ask the player to say "your turn" or "done".
The tool appears in the tool list.

items.title: Waiting does not keep a hosted game alive

goal.title: Waiting does not keep a hosted game alive
criteria: A hosted wait does not move its account's last-activity time or take a place.
A hosted game left with only a waiting assistant expires after the same idle time as a game with no assistant, and the waiting assistant is told the game expired.
Every other tool still counts as activity, as today.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/usergames/mcp.go:39-49 ResolveMCPQuiet calls r.Get(acct), not r.Use, and never sets holds or last. usergames.go:155-166 Get only creates the entry and runs expireIfIdle, so it neither moves e.last nor takes a place. The wait itself (internal/game/presence.go:284-429 Wait) does not touch the registry. internal/usergames/mcp_test.go:68-110 TestResolveMCPQuietIsNotActivity checks LastActive is unchanged and holds is false after a quiet lookup. Note: the wait machinery (presence.go, mcpserver/wait.go) and changes to internal/game/game.go, manager.go, reads.go, ui.go, mcpserver/server.go and webui/* sit outside the six files this item names. That is a scope concern for the caller; it does not change this verdict.

Expiry is unchanged: usergames.go:186-196 expireIfIdle expires a holding entry after cfg.Idle without activity, and a quiet lookup never refreshes e.last, so a waiting-only game expires at the same idle time. expireIfIdle calls M.Expire, which calls presenceRef().cleared() (game/manager.go Expire hunk), and cleared() ends the session with EndGameExpired (presence.go:171-179). Wait then returns WaitEnded with reason game_expired (presence.go:365-371). mcpserver/wait.go:31 maps that to "the game expired" and wait.go:84 sets Next to stop waiting. goal.title: Adjustable wait timings
criteria: With no settings given, managers use a 30-second cap, a five-minute check-in and a two-minute lock release.
Each setting can be changed by flag or environment variable, and the flag wins over the environment.
A cap of zero, below zero or above 50 seconds, or a negative check-in or lock-release time, stops the playmat from starting with a clear message.
The daemon started by the shim, the in-process server and every hosted account's manager all use the configured values.

goal.title: Mid-turn promote and respond outcomes
criteria: When the player knocks out the assistant's Active by attack, Ability or a plain knock-out, the wait reports a promotion once. After the assistant promotes, a continuing wait goes back to waiting.

When the player plays Judge or Unfair Stamp, the wait reports the card with its name, id and text, and the assistant can then shuffle its hand into its deck and draw during the player's turn in play mode.
A card that asks nothing of the assistant's side is reported once, and a continuing wait does not report it again.
The assistant's seat can act during the player's turn in play mode only while a response is open; at any other time the turn lock refuses it as today.
Each promote and respond result's `next` line tells the assistant what to do, and to wait again afterwards.

items.title: The acting lock and opponent status on the board server

goal.title: The acting lock and opponent status on the board server
criteria: While the assistant answers a card, promotes or plays its own turn, the board refuses game actions, closing an action, checkout and rewind with an "opponent is acting" message, but still allows mode switching, the reveal toggle, replays and reads.
Once the assistant waits again or ends its turn, the player's actions work again in the same turn.

If the assistant makes no move for the lock-release time, the board unlocks by itself and shows the opponent stopped responding. An assistant that keeps moving more often than that stays locked until it finishes.
Open boards are told "waiting" while the assistant waits, and the status disappears within 60 seconds of the assistant stopping, including straight after a check-in.
In review mode with no handed-over turn, the board never refuses an action and never shows an opponent status.
Ending a turn on the board reports that the assistant is waiting when it is.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/webui/actions.go:141-143 refuses every verb not in lookVerbs (line 112-115: set_reveal, set_mode, replay, search_deck, deck_list, look_top) while s.M.Locked(), with the opponent-acting error. end_action, checkout, rewind, draw, move and end_turn all fall under that refusal. The lock is set by presence.go:440-462 (Locked/AssistantMoved) from a card answer (WaitRespond) or promote (WaitPromote) via the defer at presence.go:550-565, and from the assistant's own-turn writes via mcpserver/server.go verb() (AssistantMoved(true) when mode is play and Current is the assistant's seat). internal/webui/lock_test.go:136-212 (TestLockRefusesGameActions) exercises both halves.

A new Wait call clears the lock at presence.go:542 (p.clearActingLocked()) before it runs. The assistant's end_turn calls AssistantDone() (mcpserver/server.go end_turn handler, after s.verb) which clears acting at presence.go:466-475.
